source: Exact current-task local conversation question calls and explicit replies only. Original line hashes are bound; no volatile whole-file hash, reasoning or unrelated message content is exposed.

questions.title: For Chapter 1 equations (1.2)–(1.3), should I adopt the explicit convention described above—geometric translation for every real profile, classical solutions for differentiable profiles, and rectangle conservation for locally integrable profiles—or retain the original analytic-scope question as unresolved? Either way, I’ll preserve the source ambiguity and continue the other obligations.
options: Adopt the explicit convention and audit under that recorded interpretation
Keep the analytic scope unresolved; record the precise proved statements separately

questions.title: For Chapter 1’s discontinuity discussion around (1.10), should the audit use this explicit interpretation: rectangle conservation, with the mass-rate identity almost everywhere in time for each fixed spatial interval, and classical solutionhood requiring spatial state differentiability? The general comparison now compiles, but the printed source leaves these conventions implicit. This is separate from your adopted convention for (1.2)–(1.3).
options: Adopt this interpretation and preserve the source ambiguity
Keep this interpretation unresolved while other Chapter 1 work continues

questions.title: Should the left-moving acoustic mode use your adopted profile convention too: geometric translation for every real profile, classical solutions for differentiable profiles, and rectangle conservation for locally integrable profiles? The audit leaves this scope unresolved; I’ll preserve both the source ambiguity and its printed switch from w² to q².
options: Apply the convention to the left-moving mode
Leave this interpretation unresolved

questions.title: For the general eigenvalue propagation claim on Chapter 1 pages 1–3, should I audit under an explicit classical interpretation: solutions jointly differentiable in space and time on ℝ², with a complete real eigenbasis and reconstruction from translated components? The theorem compiles; the audit leaves the source’s intended regularity unresolved. I’ll preserve that ambiguity and keep nonsmooth profile results separately scoped.
options: Adopt this classical interpretation
Leave this interpretation unresolved

questions.title: For the material-interface discussion on Chapter 1 page 8, should I use this explicit interpretation: both the medium and initial state have distinct left and right limits at the same interface; the initial state retains Riemann half-line data, while the medium may vary away from the interface? A compiled draft covers this and the piecewise homogeneous special case. The source leaves the medium’s global profile implicit.
options: Adopt the local-interface interpretation and preserve the ambiguity
Require the medium to be constant on each half-line
Leave this scope unresolved

questions.title: For Chapter 1’s source-term claim on page 4, should the audit use locally integrable production densities and rectangle balance, allowing either production or depletion? The compiled draft covers discontinuous states and detects nonconservation through a nonzero integrated source contribution. This interpretation excludes singular production measures; the source does not specify that boundary.
options: Adopt this density interpretation and preserve the source ambiguity
Include singular production measures
Leave the source-domain question unresolved

questions.title: For Chapter 1’s finite-volume accuracy discussion on page 5, should the audit interpret approximation through explicit bounds on the old cell-average error and the time-averaged face-flux errors, with the new cell-average error derived from them? The compiled result allows arbitrary bounds and selects no tolerance or convergence order; the source states accuracy only qualitatively.
options: Adopt this conditional error interpretation and preserve the source ambiguity
Keep accuracy qualitative and leave its analytic interpretation unresolved

questions.title: For page 8’s material-parameter averaging claim, should the audit use normalized volume averages of integrable scalar or vector fields as an explicit convention, allowing cells to have either equal or different averages? The existing Lean library supports these averages. The source says “appropriate averaging” without specifying when a physical model needs another rule, such as harmonic averaging.
options: Adopt normalized volume averaging and preserve the broader source ambiguity
Keep the averaging rule unspecified and leave this interpretation unresolved

questions.title: For the Riemann-problem definition on page 5, should I record this convention: a positive-dimensional first-order system q_t + A(x,t,q)q_x = g(x,t,q), hyperbolic on its declared state domain; two constant initial states, including equal states as a degenerate case and unequal states as the jump case? This classifies problem data without claiming solution existence. The source leaves the full equation class and equal-state boundary implicit.
options: Adopt this convention and preserve both source ambiguities
Use the same equation class but require unequal initial states
Leave the definition’s scope unresolved

questions.title: For dimensional splitting on page 6, should I interpret a logically rectangular grid as coordinate-indexed cell connectivity with separately supplied physical cell volumes and shared-face normal fluxes, and splitting as successive conservative updates along those coordinate lines? The Cartesian case now compiles. This convention would preserve the source’s unspecified geometry, accuracy order, and choice of exact or approximate Riemann solver.
options: Adopt this operational interpretation and preserve the source ambiguity
Require an explicit smooth coordinate map and its metric transformations
Keep the broader logical-grid interpretation unresolved

questions.title: For Chapter 1’s Riemann-interface discussion, should the audit adopt this compiled interpretation: each admitted solver returns a space–time field with the prescribed initial states and integrable physical interface traces on every finite real time interval, and extracts its numerical flux from that same result? Approximate fields need not satisfy exact conservation; accuracy remains conditional on explicit error bounds. The source leaves this solver representation and time domain implicit, so this choice is separate from the earlier finite-volume accuracy question.
options: Adopt this interpretation and preserve the source ambiguity
Keep this interpretation unresolved
